correctness.rationale: For any simplex invariant under sigma, fixed barycentric coordinates are constant on each involution-orbit; admissible orbit-barycentres correspond exactly to vertex orbits of diameter <=2, and a collection is a simplex iff every original pair of vertices across their union has Hamming distance <=2. This is a flag complex with 8*2^(n-4) eligible orbit vertices. Inspected verification source constructs these original orbits independently of a four-bit prefix/tail factorization, enumerates all maximal cliques and complete face sets and lexicographic matched pairs, checks all Hasse incidences for acyclicity, then eliminates unit integral Morse boundaries, giving critical vectors (1,1), (1,1,4), (1,1,20), (1,1,68,4) with zero integral differential. Independent separately coded exhaustive orbit graph and GF(2) boundary ranks reproduced face vectors (8,16,8), (16,52,48,8), (32,152,208,84,16), (64,416,768,512,192,32) and the same reduced mod-2 Betti ranks. Morse CW n4..6 with one 1-cell has trivial 2-cell attaching degrees, hence the asserted S1/S2 wedges; n7 has pi1=Z with 3-cell higher attachments left unclassified. Coordinate truncation and zero-padding commute with sigma, are 1-Lipschitz and give a simplicial retraction and section in every n>=k>=4, so only the claimed split summands follow for n>=7.
residual_risks: The original integral matching verification code was reviewed but not independently reimplemented entirely; unit-incidence Morse matching and zero integral differential are reproducible finite certificate claims.
